questions.question: Describe a Spark/PySpark pipeline you built to transform high-volume data across enterprise or application-specific layers. How did you structure the transformations and optimize performance?

What data-quality checks have you implemented in production pipelines, such as row-count, schema, or hash-key validation? How did you handle failures and prevent bad data from reaching downstream consumers?
This role uses Azure Databricks and Azure Data Factory. Based on your Spark and cloud pipeline experience, how would you design an ingestion-to-curated-data pipeline using these services?
Tell me about a fault-tolerant, scalable data-processing integration you built or operated on AWS. What were the failure scenarios, and how did the design recover from them?
How have you used Git and Jenkins to build, test, and deploy data-engineering code? Describe your branching, review, and release approach.
Describe a difficult Spark or Hive performance issue you investigated. What evidence did you use to identify the root cause, and what changes improved the workload?

When combining data from multiple source systems and platforms to produce canonical business metrics, how do you define the metric logic, resolve source inconsistencies, and ensure the result remains trusted over time?
Describe your experience scheduling and orchestrating dependent data workloads with Oozie. How would you translate that approach to production orchestration in Azure Data Factory?
Give an example of a production data-pipeline incident you diagnosed using monitoring tools such as Splunk. What was the root cause, immediate mitigation, and permanent resolution?

How would you design a Spark-based pipeline that ingests data from both relational sources and a NoSQL or event-streaming source, supports analytics and reporting, and can be tested and deployed through CI/CD?
